correctness.rationale: With a frozen error and T independent draws, each count has second moment T p_i+T(T-1)p_i^2. Expanding coordinate squares gives the exact conditional change -beta T(2U-beta V), hence the single-batch strict-descent criterion. For uniform probabilities V/U=1+(T-1)/m and U=||x||^2/m; iteration yields the exact factor and excludes nonzero starts at or above the mean-square boundary. For positive ell, the weights and squared errors are ordered together, giving U>=||x||^2/m by the pairwise covariance identity. Since V<=TU, beta T<2 gives the claimed geometric mean-square bound, hence almost-sure convergence by summable Markov bounds. At equality an axis start is a deterministic sign flip. Above it, on the path selecting one initially nonzero coordinate in every draw, probability of another all-i batch is (1+C R^(-ell k))^-T, where R=beta T-1>1. The sum of the negative logarithms is bounded by TC/(1-R^(-ell)), so this infinite event has positive probability and supplies an exponentially growing lower bound on the second moment for every nonzero start. For the stated m=4,T=3,beta=1 example the uniform factor is 5/8, while beta T=3 lies in the adaptive divergent regime.
residual_risks: No characterization of all adaptive critical trajectories, of uniform almost-sure behavior outside the mean-square range, or of nonfrozen asynchronous schedules is inferred. Finite enumeration cannot validate the infinite event by itself.

value.rationale: Holding the update schedule fixed isolates a genuine stability discontinuity between exact uniform selection and arbitrarily weak positive residual weighting. The all-start escape result rules out interpreting the instability as an artifact of starting on a single coordinate. The classification gives exact limits in a meaningful frozen model and separates positive-probability divergence and second-moment blowup from typical-trajectory or hardware performance claims.
residual_risks: The escape-event probability may be tiny; the thresholds do not characterize typical performance or general asynchronous Kaczmarz.
